output.diagnosis: Payer asserts in writing that this invoice was already settled in a batch transfer covering several bills, and offers to resend the bank advice reference. Ledger still shows the full amount outstanding, so the two records disagree. Payer notes also record irritation at repeated reminders and a stated intention to route further chasing to their legal desk. Payment history shows consistent full settlement, though typically several weeks past terms, so the claim is not implausible; it is also not proof the balance is zero.
output.reasoning: This is a remittance-matching question, not ordinary lateness. The payer has named a specific bank advice they can resend, and only a human can pull that advice and reconcile it against the batch of bills referenced. Another automated chase would repeat contact that has already produced friction and no new evidence, and the record shows the payer has asked for reminders to stop pending a check. A reminder or payment link risks demanding settlement of something that may already be paid. There is no promise-to-pay phrase and no stated payment cycle to wait on, and the receivable is substantial, so pausing silently is also unsuitable. Uncertainty: the snapshot contains no proof of receipt on our side, so the payer's claim remains unverified.
